title: Shafa‘ah, Mizan and the Sirat bridge
intro: Intercession, the scales of deeds and the bridge – what awaits us on the Last Day.

learn.html: Shafa‘ah means asking Allah to forgive someone or to raise them. On the Last Day, by Allah’s permission, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) will intercede for the believers of his ummah. Others may intercede too – prophets, martyrs, the Qur’an itself for those who recited it – but only with Allah’s permission.

On the Last Day Allah will set up the Mizan – the scales – and weigh our deeds with complete justice. No one will be wronged in the least. (Qur’an, Al-Anbiya 21:47) Whose good deeds are heavier will be successful.

learn.title: Heavy on the scales
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said that nothing is heavier on the scales than good character. Two light phrases are heavy on the scales: Subhaanallaahi wa bihamdihi, subhaanallaahil-‘Azeem. (Bukhari)
The Sirat is a bridge over Jahannam that every person must cross. People cross it according to their deeds: some like lightning, some like the wind, some running, some walking, some crawling.

items.label: Al-Hawd – the Prophet’s pool; whoever drinks from it is never thirsty again

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Our deeds today decide how heavy our scales are and how fast we cross the Sirat. Let’s send salawat on the Prophet (SAW) and hope for his intercession.

practice.title: Match the word and its meaning
Heavy on the scales
practice.prompt: Tap every deed that makes our good scale heavier, then tap Check.

options.why: That is a bad deed – it makes the other side heavier.
Lying is a sin – it does not add to our good deeds.
